title: fact-category-pin-lint CI guard mutation-tested: catches the exact D1 defect class it claims to enforce
claim_under_test: CLAUDE.md §N.7 item 2 / check_fact_category_pinning.py: a Python SELECT against chart_facts filtered by fact_category alone (no fact_key pin, no ORDER BY...LIMIT 1, no DISTINCT ON) is permanently caught by CI.
method: Injected a throwaway file (platform/python-sidecar/pp2_audit_throwaway_fact_pin_mutation.py) containing the exact D1 defect shape: `SELECT fact_id, fact_value, fact_subject FROM chart_facts WHERE chart_id = %s AND ayanamsha_id = %s AND fact_category = 'ganita.dasha_lord'` followed by client-side `rows[0]` reduction — no fact_key pin, no ORDER BY, no DISTINCT ON. Ran the exact CI invocation (.github/workflows/ci.yml lines 573-585: self-test then default repo scan) before and after the mutation, then fully reverted.
result: RED confirmed: repo-scan exit code 1, correctly flagged at the exact injected file:line (platform/python-sidecar/pp2_audit_throwaway_fact_pin_mutation.py:20) with the correct message. self-test remained exit 0 throughout (hermetic fixtures unaffected by the live-tree mutation, as designed). GREEN confirmed after revert: self-test exit 0, repo-scan exit 0 ("0 new violations (29 pre-existing, allowlisted). PASS."), git status --porcelain matched the pre-mutation baseline (only node_modules untracked).
verdict: COMPLIANT — the guard is a real, working detector, not a null check. It genuinely distinguishes the injected violation from the 29 pre-existing allowlisted violations (correctly does not double-count or misclassify), and correctly separates hermetic self-test fixtures from the live-tree scan.

title: Orchestrator asset_throughput.state='lit' no-op-completion guard (confirmed §N.8 instance #4) verified still fixed
summary: For writers with has_substeps=true, a 0-row-this-run promotion to 'lit' is gated on a genuine re-probe: writer.plan_substeps(ctx) is re-invoked inside a savepoint and remaining_count == 0 is required before final_state='lit'; otherwise an asset.noop_completion_rejected event is emitted and the asset is left 'incomplete', blocking downstream deps. This is the exact SATYA-DIPA fix CLAUDE.md §N.8 instance #4 describes and it is confirmed still present (not reverted) in asset_runner.py.

title: VIOLATION — mimamsa_insight_get's leakage_status is a hardcoded literal 'clean' with zero detector behind it
summary: grep of mi_darshana.py confirms the bare Python string literal "clean" is written at every one of 6 INSERT call sites for the leakage_status column — no variable, no conditional, no detector of any kind computes this value; it cannot ever read anything else. Live-confirmed: every one of 15 inspected insight_unit rows served for chart 482012f1 (spanning insight_type=retrodiction, verdict_object, and load_bearing) reads leakage_status='clean' identically. This is the same defect class as the four confirmed §N.8 instances (a flag with no code path that could ever produce a different value). It is materially more serious than a routine finding because leakage_status specifically claims train/test-leakage cleanliness on BLIND RETRODICTION rows (T-90d cutoff insight_units) — the entire epistemic value of a retrodiction test rests on the cutoff genuinely excluding future information, and this is precisely the row type where an unearned 'clean' claim does the most damage to the calibration story. The correct pattern already exists in the codebase one file over: mi_adhilepa.py:156-163 uses the honest 'not_assessed' tier for the identical leakage_status concept, with a code comment stating in so many words that 'clean' is reserved for when a real detector exists and passes (migration 549_adhilepa_leakage_not_assessed.sql codifies the same honest-tier convention). mi_darshana.py does not follow its sibling writer's own documented convention.
recommendation: Either (a) implement a real leakage detector for mi_darshana insight units analogous to mi_adhilepa's gated design, or (b) until one exists, emit the honest 'not_assessed' tier mi_adhilepa already established as this codebase's convention for exactly this situation — never a bare 'clean' literal with no check behind it.

title: Contrast case — mi_adhilepa's leakage tier correctly uses the honest 'not_assessed' null value
summary: Included as the direct positive contrast to W3-F-102. Code comment at mi_adhilepa.py:156-163 states explicitly: "leakage='not_assessed' until a real [detector exists]... 'clean' is reserved for when a real leakage detector exists and passes." This is the textbook-correct application of CLAUDE.md §N.7 item 6 ('an honest null beats an invented judgment') for the identical concept that mi_darshana (W3-F-102) gets wrong.

title: bodha_quality_get defect_001 status is re-derived live via real SQL on every call, not a stored/stale value
summary: deriveDefect001Note() runs a live SQL LEFT JOIN counting constituent_facts_array references against chart_facts.fact_id on every single call — never a cached/stored value — with genuine thresholds (0% orphan -> RESOLVED, <5% -> MOSTLY_RESOLVED, else -> OPEN) and an honest UNKNOWN fallback if the live query itself fails ('cannot derive an orphan rate; not asserting one'). Live-observed: status='MOSTLY_RESOLVED', metrics={total_refs:71967, orphan_refs:49, orphan_pct:0.1} for chart 482012f1, consistent with the thresholds. The served scorecard.unresolved_constituent_facts_count is explicitly overwritten with this same live-derived count specifically so the two numbers cannot disagree — a documented GA.1-class registry-disagreement fix.
